q-79667.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $x+5≡11\,(\text{mod}\,15)?$
q-79667.worked_solution:
The addition property of congruences states that

$$
a≡b\,⟺\,a+c≡b+c\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

$$
a≡b\,⟺\,a-c≡b-c\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5 & ≡11\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x+5-5 & ≡11-5\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}
$$

q-79657.name: Question 11
q-79657.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $x≡7\,(\text{mod}\,12)?$
q-79657.worked_solution:
When we add zero to both sides of a congruence modulo $n$, we can form an equivalent congruence by writing zero as an integer multiple of $n.$ This works because every integer multiple of $n$ is congruent to zero modulo $n.$

In our case, we add zero to both sides of the congruence and then use the fact that  $12\cdot 2≡0\,(\text{mod}\,12)$ to rewrite the right-hand side, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+0 & ≡7+0\, & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ x & ≡7+0\, & (\text{mod}\,12) \\  & ≡7+12\cdot 2\, & (\text{mod}\,12) \\  & ≡7+24\, & (\text{mod}\,12) \\  & ≡31\, & (\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

q-212906.name: Question 16
q-212906.problem:
The United States Declaration of Independence was ratified on July 4th, 1776. Given that January 1st, 1776, was a Monday, use congruences to determine on which day of the week the Declaration of Independence was ratified.

*Hint: The year 1776 was a leap year since it's divisible by $4$ and is not an end-of-century year.*
q-212906.worked_solution:
We can solve this problem using modular arithmetic.

First, we note the number of complete months between January 1st, 1776, and July 1st, 1776. 

- There were $3$ months with $31$ days (January, March, and May).

- There were $2$ months with $30$ days (April, and June).

- There was $1$ month with $29$ days (February) since it was a leap year.

Therefore, the number of days $d$ between January 1st and July 4th is given by

$$
d=\overset{\text{days to July 1st}}{\overset{⏞}{31(3)+30(2)+29(1)}}+3.
$$

Now, note that

$$
31≡3,\,30≡2,\,29≡1,\,(\text{mod}\,7).
$$

Therefore, writing the number $d$ modulo $7,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =3(31)+2(30)+1(29)+3 \\  & ≡3(3)+2(2)+1(1)+3\, & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡9+4+1+3\, & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡2+4+1+3\, & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡10\, & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the day of the week is the same as the date $3$ days after January 1st, 1776, namely Thursday.
